version.changelog:
web-slides 2.0.0

- Major overhaul: Clearer positioning as the best choice for premium, single-file HTML slides with mobile-optimized themes and zero API dependencies.
- Comprehensive SKILL.md rewrite: Now details guiding principles, decision workflows, quality standards, theme and layout selection, and output rules.
- Model-agnostic by design: Never assumes specific LLM or vendor capabilities; focuses purely on local scripts, themes, and layout systems.
- Emphasizes polished, high-end output with strict mobile compatibility—all without sacrificing token efficiency.
- Offers command scripts for rapid prototyping, validation, theme selection, and streamlined generation.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-slides
Version: 2.0.0

The skill bundle is a sophisticated tool for generating themed HTML slide decks from Markdown or JSON. It is classified as suspicious because it utilizes the `node:child_process` module to execute system commands and external binaries, specifically invoking Google Chrome in headless mode to render PNG previews (found in `scripts/chrome-utils.mjs` and `scripts/render-preview.mjs`). While these high-risk capabilities are plausibly required for the stated purpose of generating presentation previews, the ability to execute arbitrary local binaries and access the filesystem via shell commands warrants caution. No evidence of intentional malice, data exfiltration, or obfuscation was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, files, and runtime instructions are consistent with a local, model‑agnostic HTML slide generator that uses bundled templates and Node scripts; nothing requests unrelated credentials or external endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description (generate single‑file HTML slide decks) matches the included scripts, theme files, and references. It is reasonable that local Node scripts, templates, and theme markdown are present. Minor mismatch: the package declares no required binaries/env but several scripts assume a Node runtime (they are .mjs) and an optional headless Chrome (chrome-utils.mjs uses a Mac Chrome path and CHROME_BIN). These are implementation details rather than indicators of malicious intent, but they are practical requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read only the included references and run local scripts (generate, scaffold, validate, render, etc.). The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files, secrets, or call external HTTP endpoints. The scripts operate on local files and produce HTML/PNG outputs as described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and all code is bundled with the skill (instruction‑only install). No downloads or external installers are used. Scripts are local .mjs files and will be executed by Node — no remote fetch or archive extraction was found in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, and indeed no sensitive secrets are requested. One optional env var is referenced in chrome-utils.mjs (CHROME_BIN) to override a default Chrome binary path; this is reasonable for preview rendering but should be noted by users. No other unrelated environment variables or config paths are accessed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It writes output files into local paths like dist/, which is normal for a generator. The ability to execute scripts (child_process.execFileSync) is present but used to run bundled Node scripts and optionally Chrome for rendering previews — expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and implements a local Node-based slide generator using bundled templates and scripts. Before installing or granting execution rights: 1) be aware the scripts execute Node (.mjs) files and spawn processes (execFileSync); ensure you run them in a trusted or sandboxed environment if you are not comfortable. 2) Preview rendering optionally invokes headless Chrome; if you need that feature, ensure Node and Chrome (or set CHROME_BIN) are available. 3) The skill writes outputs (dist/, preview PNGs, manifests) to the working directory — review those artifacts and the scripts (especially generate-slide-html.mjs and chrome-utils.mjs) if you want to be extra cautious. 4) No network calls or secret-exfiltration patterns were found in the provided files, and no environment variables or external API keys are required. If you need higher assurance, run the scripts in an isolated environment or audit the remaining truncated files not included here.
